name: National Coastal Resilience Fund
summary: Annual grants for planning, design and implementation of nature-based solutions, such as marsh, dune, reef and floodplain restoration, that reduce coastal hazard risks to communities in U.S. coastal areas while improving fish and wildlife habitat.

geography.label: Coastal areas of U.S. coastal and Great Lakes states, U.S. territories and Tribal lands

reporting: Grantees submit interim programmatic reports every 6 months (restoration implementation) or annually (planning and design), periodic fiscal reports, and a final programmatic report about 3 months after the grant ends.

eligibility.rule: Locate the project in eligible coastal areas of U.S. states, territories or Tribal lands
Demonstrate benefits to both coastal communities and habitats
Show clear benefits that reduce current and projected threats to communities from coastal hazards
Improve habitats for fish and wildlife species
Include a year of post-construction monitoring for Restoration Implementation projects
Include restoration work beyond monitoring alone for Restoration Implementation projects
Not a federal agency, foreign organization, foreign public entity or unincorporated individual

documents: Pre-Proposal Special Upload, if seeking equipment funding

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state and territorial government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations, educational institutions, or commercial (for-profit) organizations.

geography.quote: Projects must be located within the coastal areas of U.S. coastal states, including the Great Lakes states, and U.S. territories and Tribal lands.

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

window.quote: NOAA staff are also consulted on program priorities and goals for the fund's development, the annual call for proposal, and in proposal review

co_finance_required.quote: Non-federal match is not required but encouraged.

reporting.quote: We require interim programmatic reports every 6 months for Restoration Implementation projects and annually for planning and design projects.

eligibility.quote: Projects must be located within the coastal areas of U.S. coastal states, including the Great Lakes states, and U.S. territories and Tribal lands.
All projects under this program must demonstrate benefits to both coastal communities and habitats.
Projects must show clear benefits in terms of reducing current and projected threats to communities from coastal hazards
Projects must improve habitats for fish and wildlife species.
Applicants under this category are requesting funds to construct a restoration project and projects MUST include a year of post-construction monitoring to assess the outcomes of the project.
Projects that conduct monitoring only are not eligible.
Ineligible applicants include federal agencies or employees of federal agencies, foreign organizations, foreign public entities, and unincorporated individuals.

after_award.quote: We require interim programmatic reports every 6 months for Restoration Implementation projects and annually for planning and design projects. We also require periodic fiscal reporting (from quarterly to annually), depending on the organization and the size and complexity of the award.

documents.quote: Pre-Proposal Narrative: The most important upload is your actual pre-proposal narrative.
Applicants seeking funding for equipment must complete a separate Pre-Proposal Special Upload describing the need to purchase equipment.
